note: Attacker-controlled UART bytes enter the HDLC decoder as the raw input stream.

code: ReadUtf8 returns a pointer to a NUL-terminated string inside the decoded Spinel frame.
note: The decoder exposes the first UTF-8 field from the frame as passPhrase without copying or length bounding beyond NUL termination.
The attacker-controlled passphrase is consumed as the first argument to the commissioner PSKC generation path.
A second attacker-controlled UTF-8 string is parsed and later appended into the PBKDF2 salt.
The extended PAN ID bytes are read from the same attacker-controlled frame and validated only for exact length.
The three attacker-controlled fields are forwarded into the commissioner implementation.
The API wrapper passes the raw pointers directly to the core PSKC generator.

code: memcpy(salt, saltPrefix, strlen(saltPrefix)); memcpy(salt + saltLen, aExtPanId.m8, sizeof(aExtPanId)); memcpy(salt + saltLen, aNetworkName, strlen(aNetworkName));
note: The vulnerable root cause is a stack-buffer-overflow write: the fixed-size local salt buffer is extended with attacker-controlled networkName bytes without checking that saltLen stays within OT_PBKDF2_SALT_MAX_LEN, so a long network name overflows the stack buffer before PBKDF2 runs.
